idiom_name: class bundling data and behaviour; module boundary with underscore conventions
implementation_notes: Python's class already is the concept: methods defined in the class body receive self and own the state, properties turn computed rules into attribute reads, and @dataclass generates only the plumbing while domain operations stay in the same class. Privacy is conventional - a single leading underscore marks non-public attributes (PEP 8), name mangling with double underscores exists to avoid subclass collisions, not for security - and stateless behaviour dissolves into module-level functions, which is the honest alternative when no invariant is involved.
pitfalls: Nothing is private: the underscore conventions are documentation, so invariants rely on discipline and review - clients can still reach _lines.
@dataclass-generated __init__/__eq__ encourage a field bag; keep domain operations in the class instead of growing an InvoiceService module beside it.
Spreading one concept over modules that reference each other creates circular imports; one concept per module keeps the import graph acyclic.
